#### 1. multiple congenital anomalies-hypotonia-seizures syndrome 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.715)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-162710)

**Proposed mechanism:** PIGA (HGNC:8957) —DISRUPTS→ GPI anchor biosynthesis (GO:0006494); GPI anchor biosynthesis (GO:0006494) —LEADS_TO→ Complement-mediated cell lysis (HP:0001897); GPI anchor biosynthesis (GO:0006494) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252); GPI anchor biosynthesis (GO:0006494) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); GPI anchor biosynthesis (GO:0006494) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital anomalies (HP:0000118). Loss-of-function mutations in PIGA impair the initiation of GPI anchor biosynthesis. This deficiency affects multiple downstream cellular processes, leading to complement-mediated cell lysis characteristic of PNH1, and a spectrum of neurological and developmental abnormalities, including hypotonia, seizures, and congenital anomalies seen in MCAHS2.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with PIGA variants that lead to a detectable, albeit reduced, functional GPI anchor biosynthesis pathway, and who do not exhibit the core phenotypes of either PNH1 or MCAHS2. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing a common, benign variant in PIGA with a frequency > 0.1% that does not disrupt GPI anchor biosynthesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of PIGA and GPI anchor biosynthesis in these distinct diseases offers potential therapeutic avenues. Strategies aimed at restoring GPI anchor synthesis or mitigating downstream effects could be broadly applicable to both PNH1 and MCAHS2, potentially leading to novel treatments for rare genetic disorders.
